title: Modular exponentiation invariant
statement: For Boolean lists $z$ and $S$, let $a$, $e$, and $m$ be the natural numbers encoded by the first component of $z$, the first component of its second component, and the second component of its second component. The state $S$ encodes lists $E$, $b$, and $\mathrm{acc}$ in the form specified by the pair encoding, where $E$ has length at most the length of the binary representation of $e$, $b$ and $\mathrm{acc}$ are canonical binary representations, $b$ has length at most the sum of the lengths of the binary representations of $a$ and $m$, and $\mathrm{acc}$ has length at most one plus the length of the binary representation of $m$. If $m>0$, then $b$ and $\mathrm{acc}$ encode numbers less than $m$, and $\mathrm{acc}\,b^{\mathrm{val}(E)}$ is congruent to $a^e$ modulo $m$.
hypotheses_covered: There exist lists $E$, $b$, and $\mathrm{acc}$ giving the specified encoded state
$E$ has length at most the length of the encoded exponent
When the encoded modulus is positive, both encoded values are less than the modulus and satisfy the stated modular congruence
caveat: The snippet does not define the pair encoding or binary-value function, so these representations and values can only be described using their evident roles.
